title: Quick check: UI Consistency and Design Systems

questions.prompt: In the context of “UI Consistency and Design Systems” and “Component APIs”, What is the main advantage of a CSS Module such as `Card.module.css`?
options: It makes every class global across all websites.
It runs database queries in the browser.
Its generated class names are scoped to reduce accidental style collisions.
It automatically makes an interface accessible without semantic markup.
questions.answer_key: Its generated class names are scoped to reduce accidental style collisions.
questions.explanation: CSS Modules provide locally scoped class names; they do not replace semantic HTML or accessibility testing.

questions.prompt: While implementing “UI Consistency and Design Systems”, Which approach is a good starting point for responsive layout?
options: Use flexible layouts and mobile-first styles, then add breakpoints when content needs them.
Set a fixed desktop width for every viewport.
Use color alone to convey every status.
Hide all keyboard focus indicators to save space.
questions.answer_key: Use flexible layouts and mobile-first styles, then add breakpoints when content needs them.
questions.explanation: Responsive layouts adapt to available space; test real content, text scaling, and keyboard use at multiple sizes.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “UI Consistency and Design Systems”, What should a shared design system define?
options: A different arbitrary spacing value for each page.
Unreviewed global overrides for every component.
Consistent tokens and component patterns for typography, spacing, states, and accessible controls.
Only screenshots without component behavior or documentation.
questions.answer_key: Consistent tokens and component patterns for typography, spacing, states, and accessible controls.
questions.explanation: Design tokens and documented component APIs help keep UI behavior and appearance consistent.
